rule: Size every HBM<->SBUF DMA so each partition moves at least 2 KiB of contiguous data, targeting 4 KiB or more.
why: Each DMA transfer pays fixed descriptor-setup, synchronization and semaphore-to-start costs; below ~2 KiB per partition the DMA packet rate, not HBM bandwidth, limits throughput. At 4096 free bytes the DMA curve nearly saturates.
trigger: A dma_copy/nl.load whose free-dim bytes per partition are < 2048 (fp32 < 512 elems, bf16 < 1024 elems, fp8 < 2048 elems).
fix: Widen the free dimension of the DMA tile (coalesce adjacent sub-tiles into one transfer) until bytes/partition >= 4096.
check_sketch: for each dma op: bytes_per_partition = prod(free_shape)*dtype_bytes; flag if < 2048; warn if < 4096.

rule: Spread every DMA across all 128 SBUF partitions so all 16 DMA engines participate.
why: Each DMA engine serves a fixed group of 8 SBUF partitions (128/16); a transfer touching only P partitions uses ceil(P/8) engines. A [4,4096] bf16 load used 1 engine and took 1416 ns for 32 KiB while 15 engines idled.
trigger: dma_copy whose SBUF-side partition count is far below 128 (e.g. 4, 16, 32).
fix: Reshape the transfer so the partition dimension is 128 (e.g. view [4,4096] as [128,128]) or batch several small tensors into one 128-partition tile.
check_sketch: for each dma op touching SBUF: engines_used = ceil(P/8); flag if P < 128 and the transfer is on the critical path.

rule: Budget memory-bound kernels against per-core DMA bandwidth: 16 engines x 23 B/ns = 368 GB/s on Trainium2.
why: Each NeuronCore is paired with 16 DMA engines; each engine moves one transfer at a time at a fixed peak rate (17 B/ns trn1, 23 B/ns trn2, 33 B/ns trn3). Per-engine theoretical peak is also quoted as 27.2 GB/s (v2/v3) and 38.4 GB/s (v4).
trigger: Estimating the lower bound of a weight-streaming kernel's runtime, or checking achieved MBU.
fix: Runtime_lower_bound = bytes_moved / 368e9 on trn2 per core; if achieved is far above this, apply the payload-size and partition rules.
check_sketch: runtime_lb = total_dma_bytes / (16*23e9); report achieved/lb ratio.
source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dma-bandwidth-guide.rst :: Why Large Contiguous DMA Payloads Are Required; nki/get-started/about/nki-dma-overview.rst :: Basic DMA Capabilities / Performance Considerations

rule: Make each DMA transfer (per engine) at least 32 KiB; a 128x1024 fp32 load maps to 16 transfers of 32 KiB each.
why: The compiler splits one nl.load into up to 16 DMA transfers (one per engine), each a scatter-gather list of 8 partition buffers. Transfer-level overhead is amortized only when each transfer is large; 32 B transfers seen in profiles were overhead-dominated.
trigger: Profile DMA-per-engine view shows gaps longer than active bars, or hover shows tiny transfer sizes (e.g. 32 B).
fix: Load [128, 1024] fp32 (or equivalent bytes) per nl.load; beyond 1024 fp32 elements per partition returns diminish and pipelining suffers.
check_sketch: transfer_bytes = (P/16)*free_bytes; flag if < 32768.
source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #9: Perform sufficiently large DMA transfers

rule: Treat every DMA transfer as costing ~1300 ns of cross-engine synchronization before data moves; amortize it with large payloads.
why: Each DMA transfer involves descriptor setup, synchronization and semaphore-to-start latency (~1300 ns cross-engine). Small transfers make the engine spend more time on overhead than data.
trigger: Many small DMAs in the inner loop; DMA active time high but MBU < 60%.
fix: Coalesce into fewer, larger DMAs; prefetch a block ahead so the fixed latency overlaps compute.
check_sketch: per_dma_cost = 1300ns + bytes/(23 B/ns); flag loops where overhead term > 30% of total.

rule: Issue one DMA covering multiple logical sub-tiles instead of many DMAs to adjacent addresses.
why: Per-packet overhead is fixed per DMA; one large transfer to contiguous addresses fills the engine pipelines, many small ones do not.
trigger: A loop issuing dma_copy per 128x128 tile where the tiles are contiguous in HBM.
fix: Allocate an SBUF tile [128, k*F] and load k adjacent HBM sub-tiles in a single dma_copy; the kernel-optimization tutorial loads [TILE_K, BLOCK_N] rhs blocks and packs [TILE_M, BLOCK_N] results before storing.
check_sketch: detect consecutive dma ops whose HBM ranges are adjacent and destinations are adjacent in SBUF; suggest merge.

rule: Do not expect HBM channel interleaving to rescue small or fragmented DMA transfers.
why: Interleaving only spreads traffic across HBM channels; it does not reduce packet count or per-packet overhead, so packets-per-second limits remain.
trigger: Reasoning that strided/fragmented access is fine because the memory system interleaves.
fix: Fix payload size and partition coverage at the kernel level.

rule: Lay out HBM tensors so each DMA reads sequential addresses; keep strided/gather access to the SBUF free dimension instead.
why: HBM is linear memory and is always more performant when accessed sequentially; SBUF/PSUM free-dim striding is cheap. Each non-contiguous HBM run becomes a separate DMA buffer with its own overhead.
trigger: nl.load with a strided or permuted HBM index pattern, or an HBM layout whose minor dim is not the SBUF free dim.
fix: Choose kernel IO layouts so the HBM minor dimension maps to the SBUF free dimension; reorder data on-chip with access patterns.
check_sketch: for dma ops: inspect HBM-side pattern; flag if innermost step != 1 or run length*dtype < 2 KiB.
source: nki/get-started/about/indexing-overview.rst :: Basic Tensor Indexing; nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Data movement between HBM and SBUF using DMAs

rule: Expect at least P DMA buffers (one per partition) for any SBUF-side transfer, plus more if the per-partition free slice is non-contiguous.
why: SBUF addresses increment along the free dimension then advance to the next partition, so partition slices are non-contiguous in the address map; each contiguous run is a DMA buffer with its own overhead.
trigger: Non-contiguous free-dim slices in the SBUF side of a dma_copy (e.g. strided columns).
fix: Keep the SBUF-side free slice contiguous; apply strides on compute-engine reads instead.
check_sketch: flag dma ops whose SBUF access pattern has inner step != 1.

rule: In memory-bound kernels, replace nl.load_transpose2d / DMA transposes with a plain contiguous nl.load followed by nisa.nc_transpose on TensorE.
why: DMA transpose runs at much lower DMA bandwidth than a copy (up to 90% HBM2SBUF with friendly shapes on trn2, far less otherwise; trn1 'much lower'); TensorE transpose is the fastest transpose when TensorE is idle.
trigger: Profile search for transpose DMA activities shows substantial time; kernel is DMA-bound.
fix: for i in range(N//128): tile = nl.load(x[i*128:(i+1)*128, 0:128]); out[:, i*128:(i+1)*128] = nisa.nc_transpose(tile)
check_sketch: flag dma_transpose/load_transpose2d in kernels whose dma_bytes/compute_flops indicates memory-bound.
source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #10: Minimize use of DMA transposes; nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: DMA Transpose

rule: When using nisa.dma_transpose HBM->SBUF on Trainium2, make the output partition count a multiple of 128 and the inner-most free size a multiple of 16.
why: All 16 DMA engines cooperatively write one [128, 16] SBUF tile at a time; shapes that are not multiples of 128 and 16 still work but lose DMA efficiency. Supports bit-accurate 2-byte and 4-byte dtypes.
trigger: dma_transpose with dst shape not (128k, 16m) or 1-byte dtype.
fix: Pad/tile the transpose so dst is [128*k, 16*m]; use 2- or 4-byte dtypes.
check_sketch: for dma_transpose: flag if dst.shape[0] % 128 != 0 or dst.shape[-1] % 16 != 0 or dtype_bytes not in (2,4).

rule: For decode attention, load the K cache stored as [seqlen, d_head] in HBM with an HBM2SBUF DMA transpose so d_head lands on the partition dimension for Q@K^T.
why: TensorE needs the contraction dim (d_head) on partitions; the HBM minor dim is d_head, so mapping it to partitions is exactly a DMA transpose, avoiding a TensorE transpose per K tile.
trigger: Decode-phase attention kernel where K cache layout is [seqlen, d_head] and TensorE is not the bottleneck.
fix: nisa.dma_transpose(dst=k_sbuf[d_head, seqlen_tile], src=k_hbm[seqlen_tile, d_head]) with seqlen_tile a multiple of 16 and d_head*... multiple of 128.

rule: Use SBUF->SBUF DMA transpose (nisa.dma_transpose) as the PF-transpose path in ScalarE/VectorE-bound kernels such as self-attention.
why: TensorE transpose is faster but its PSUM output must be evicted by ScalarE/VectorE; DMA transpose reads and writes SBUF directly, offloading the busy engines, at up to 50% of DMA throughput.
trigger: Profile shows VectorE/ScalarE near 100% while DMA engines have slack and transposes are needed.
fix: Replace nisa.nc_transpose(engine=tensor)+tensor_copy with nisa.dma_transpose(dst=sbuf_dst, src=sbuf_src).

rule: When casting inside a DMA (different src/dst dtypes), expect the hardware to cast src->FP32->dst; never DMA-cast MXFP4/MXFP8.
why: DMA casting is implemented as a two-step conversion through FP32, which matters for integer types; MX packed types are not supported by DMA casting.
trigger: dma_copy with src.dtype != dst.dtype, especially integer or MX types.
fix: Cast on a compute engine (tensor_copy) for integer semantics; keep MX tiles the same dtype across DMAs.
check_sketch: flag dma ops with dtype mismatch where either side is an int or an _x4 MX type.

rule: Remember that DMA transfers in the same queue on the same engine execute strictly in order; independent streams should land in different queues.
why: There are 16 DMA queues per engine; a transfer is submitted to one queue ID across all 16 engines. Queues are scheduled round-robin (v2/v3) or by QoS (v4). The queue ID is tied to the trigger engine and descriptor-generation method.
trigger: A latency-critical small DMA is stuck behind large transfers in the same queue (visible as queue name in profiler hover).
fix: Trigger the critical DMA from a different engine (hwdge engine=scalar vs sync) so it uses a different queue; keep bulk prefetch in its own queue.

rule: Account for a fixed 16 semaphore-update writes per DMA transfer regardless of how many engines carried data.
why: The NeuronCore waits for a semaphore increment of 16 to detect completion, so all 16 engines write a 4 B semaphore even when only one moved data; tiny DMAs are therefore dominated by this fixed cost.
trigger: Many very small DMAs (e.g. per-row scalar loads).
fix: Batch small loads into one wider DMA.

rule: Never DMA directly from PSUM to HBM; evict PSUM to SBUF with tensor_copy (ScalarE/VectorE) first.
why: Only compute engines read PSUM; DMA engines move between HBM and SBUF.
trigger: dma_copy whose src buffer is PSUM.
fix: nisa.tensor_copy(dst=sbuf_tmp, src=psum_tile); nisa.dma_copy(dst=hbm_out, src=sbuf_tmp)
check_sketch: flag dma ops with a PSUM operand.

rule: Treat GpSimd's eight integrated DMA engines (307 GB/s total on Trainium2) as extra bandwidth that runs in parallel with the main DMA ring and with GpSimd compute.
why: In NeuronCore-v3 each GpSimd processor has an integrated DMA engine reaching any SBUF/HBM in the instance; aggregate 153 GB/s per direction.
trigger: Main DMA queues saturated while GpSimd is idle.
fix: Let the compiler route some transfers via GpSimd (swdge-triggered DMAs run from the qGpSimdDynamic queue).

rule: On Trainium3, plan reductions that accumulate into an SBUF tile via DMA read-add-write at full copy throughput (no NKI API yet).
why: NeuronCore-v4 ReadAddWrite unit performs B += A near SBUF for BF16/FP32 (matching dtypes) at the same throughput as DMA copy, versus 50% via DMA collective-compute engines before.
trigger: Reduce-scatter-like accumulation into SBUF on trn3.
fix: Await nki.isa support; until then use tensor_tensor add on VectorE.

rule: Give every dma_copy/dma_transpose a descriptive name= string.
why: The name appears in profiler traces and compiler debug output, making it easy to attribute DMA activity to source lines.
trigger: Analyzing DMA queues in Neuron Explorer.
fix: nisa.dma_copy(dst=..., src=..., name='load_w_block_k')
check_sketch: flag dma ops without name=.

rule: Leave dge_mode at the default (unknown) until a profile shows descriptor generation is the bottleneck, then force a specific mode.
why: The compiler picks none/swdge/hwdge from target, shapes and schedule; overriding blindly can move the cost to a busier resource.
trigger: Tuning DMA-heavy kernels.
fix: Start with nisa.dma_copy(dst, src); switch to dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.hwdge or swdge only after profiling.

rule: Budget ~600 ns per hardware-DGE DMA instruction on Trainium2 and keep the number of such instructions per kernel small.
why: Each NeuronCore-v3 has two DGE instances (triggered by ScalarE or SyncE sequencer); each DGE-based DMA instruction takes about 600 ns to execute, so issuing thousands of small DMAs makes descriptor generation, not bandwidth, the bottleneck.
trigger: Memory-bound kernel with many small or strided dma_copy calls (e.g. per-token, per-head, per-block gathers).
fix: Merge DMAs into fewer, larger instructions; at 368 GB/s a 600 ns DGE slot moves ~220 KB, so transfers much smaller than that are DGE-rate bound.
check_sketch: dge_time = n_hwdge_dma_instructions * 600ns / 2 instances; flag if dge_time > bytes/368GB/s.

rule: Trigger hardware-DGE DMAs from ScalarE (engine=nisa.engine.scalar) when ScalarE has earlier independent compute, so descriptor generation hides behind it.
why: DGE and ScalarE's compute pipeline are independent resources; a DGE instruction issued from the ScalarE sequencer can execute behind earlier activate() instructions in program order. Only scalar and sync are valid trigger engines for hwdge.
trigger: hwdge DMAs sit on the critical path and ScalarE is busy with preceding work.
fix: nisa.dma_copy(dst, src, dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.hwdge, engine=nisa.engine.scalar)
check_sketch: flag hwdge dma with engine=sync when ScalarE utilization is high and there is preceding ScalarE work.

rule: Do not use hwdge for gather/scatter: any .ap() with vector_offset (or vector_select) forces swdge on GpSimd.
why: NeuronCore-v3 hardware DGE does not support indirect DMA; only software DGE on GpSimd can build descriptors from per-partition indices in SBUF.
trigger: dma_copy/dma_transpose whose src/dst carries vector_offset with dge_mode=hwdge or none.
fix: Use dge_mode=unknown or swdge for indirect transfers; where the index is a single runtime value use scalar_offset (allowed with any mode).
check_sketch: if any operand .is_indirect() with vector offset and dge_mode in (hwdge, none): error.
source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dge.rst :: How .ap() Affects DGE Mode; nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: DGE note

rule: Expect software DGE (gather/scatter, dynamic addressing) to consume GpSimd cycles and SBUF descriptor space; in GpSimd-bound kernels it becomes the bottleneck.
why: swdge generates descriptors on the GpSimd engine during execution and stores them in a portion of SBUF, competing with iota/mask/custom-op work.
trigger: Profile shows GpSimd busy with descriptor generation (DMAs triggered from qGpSimdDynamic) while DMA engines idle.
fix: Reduce indirect DMA count (gather larger contiguous blocks per index), move other GpSimd work to VectorE/ScalarE, or use scalar_offset+hwdge where the pattern allows.
source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dge.rst :: swdge / Performance Implications; nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: Descriptor Generation Engine (DGE)

rule: Prefer dge_mode=none only for fully static patterns with few DMA instances; each pre-computed descriptor consumes HBM capacity and bandwidth on first fetch.
why: Static descriptors are generated on the host at NEFF load and stored in HBM, one per DMA instruction instance; they give the lowest per-transfer latency but cannot express runtime addresses and bloat HBM for large unrolled loops.
trigger: Large unrolled static loops with thousands of DMAs on trn2.
fix: Use hwdge (on-demand, no storage) for bulk static DMAs on NeuronCore-v3+.
check_sketch: count dma ops with dge_mode none in unrolled loops; warn above a few hundred.

rule: For dma_transpose with hwdge, make src.shape[0] == 16, src.shape[-1] % 128 == 0 and dtype 2 bytes.
why: Hardware DGE transpose descriptors are fixed to the 16-row cooperative tile and 128-wide output.
trigger: dma_transpose(..., dge_mode=hwdge) with other shapes.
fix: Tile the source into [16, 128k] bf16/fp16 pieces or let the compiler choose the mode.
check_sketch: check src.shape[0]==16 and src.shape[-1]%128==0 and dtype_bytes==2.

rule: For indirect (gather) dma_transpose under swdge: src on HBM, src.shape[-1] <= 128, 2-byte dtype, src.shape[0] % 16 == 0, 2-D uint32 SBUF index tensor with shape[0] in [16,128] divisible by 16 (exactly 128 when indices.shape[1] > 1); NeuronCore-v3+ only.
why: Software DGE indirect-transpose descriptors are generated per 16-row group with a 128-wide limit.
trigger: Gather+transpose of K/V cache rows by a runtime index list.
fix: src_ap = hbm.ap(pattern=[[P,F],[1,P]], vector_offset=idx_u32, indirect_dim=0); nisa.dma_transpose(dst, src_ap, dge_mode=swdge)
check_sketch: validate the listed shape/dtype constraints.

rule: When the runtime indirection is a single offset (e.g. a block/batch index), express it with scalar_offset or .select(), which keeps hwdge/none eligible, instead of a one-element vector_offset.
why: scalar_offset is supported by every DGE mode for both dma_copy and dma_transpose; vector_offset is restricted to swdge.
trigger: Dynamic KV-cache block or batch selection implemented via vector_offset.
fix: src = A.ap(pattern=[[512,128],[1,256]], scalar_offset=idx_reg_or_1x1_tile, indirect_dim=0) or A.select(0, idx).
check_sketch: flag vector_offset whose index tensor shape is (1,1).
source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dge.rst :: How .ap() Affects DGE Mode; nki/deep-dives/nki-aps.rst :: Scalar Dynamic Access

rule: Design gather-style memory-bound kernels (paged KV, embeddings, interpolation, grid-sample) around descriptor rate: one indirect DMA per index row is swdge on GpSimd, so maximize bytes per descriptor and partitions per DMA.
why: Indirect DMAs require swdge (GpSimd generates descriptors into SBUF); hwdge is ~600 ns per instruction and cannot gather; each transfer also pays ~1300 ns sync. With rows of a few hundred bytes the kernel is bound by descriptor generation, not HBM bandwidth.
trigger: Many dma ops with vector_offset whose per-partition payload is < 2 KiB, or DMA engines idle while GpSimd/DGE queues are busy.
fix: Gather 128 rows per DMA (vector_offset of shape [128,1]) with the widest contiguous row slice possible; prefer block-contiguous layouts (e.g. page size >= 2 KiB per row group) so scalar_offset+hwdge suffices.
check_sketch: for indirect dma ops: est = max(bytes/368GB/s, n_descriptors*gpsimd_descriptor_cost); flag if descriptor term dominates.
source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dge.rst :: swdge / hwdge; nki/deep-dives/nki-dma-bandwidth-guide.rst :: Why Large Contiguous DMA Payloads Are Required; nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: DGE

rule: Read the DMA queue name in the profiler to learn how a DMA was generated: qGpSimdDynamic means swdge (GpSimd-generated), qSyncIO* static/sync-triggered, qSyncSpillReload* compiler spills.
why: The queue ID is tied to the trigger engine and the descriptor-generation method; the trigger instruction can be found on the corresponding engine trace.
trigger: Diagnosing which engine is paying for descriptor generation.
fix: Click the DMA in Neuron Explorer, note the queue, then locate the trigger instruction on that engine's trace.

rule: Capture profiles with --enable-dge-notifs to see DGE DMA events, but expect notification-queue overflow and timeouts when the kernel issues very many DGE instructions.
why: DGE DMA events are not recorded by default; the notification queue has limited capacity.
trigger: Profiling hwdge-heavy kernels.
fix: neuron-explorer capture -n graph.neff -s profile.ntff --profile-nth-exec=2 --enable-dge-notifs; drop the flag if execution times out.
source: nki/guides/use-neuron-profile.rst :: Step 3: Profile the Generated NEFF

rule: Use vector_select/vector_offset only on HBM sources with indirect_dim=0; the output partition count equals the index vector length and only one dynamic select is allowed per view.
why: Hardware indirect DMA gathers whole rows: partition p reads row offsets[p]; the leading-dim stride is taken from the base tensor shape (pattern stride ignored) and the selected dim cannot be further sliced.
trigger: Gather implemented with indirect_dim != 0 or chained selects.
fix: src = A.vector_select(0, offsets[P,1]); nisa.dma_copy(dst=sbuf[P, cols], src=src)
check_sketch: validate indirect_dim==0, source buffer is HBM, no chained select.

rule: Feed nc_matmul only from SBUF and expect its output only in PSUM.
why: TensorE streams stationary/moving operands from SBUF and writes to PSUM; it cannot read PSUM or write SBUF.
trigger: nc_matmul with a PSUM operand as input or an SBUF dst.
fix: Evict previous PSUM results to SBUF (tensor_copy) before reusing them as matmul inputs; allocate dst with buffer=nl.psum.
check_sketch: check nc_matmul operand buffers: stationary/moving in SBUF, dst in PSUM.

rule: Use VectorE or ScalarE (tensor_copy, activation, tensor_tensor, tensor_reduce) to read PSUM; TensorE is write-only to PSUM and only TensorE can trigger PSUM accumulation.
why: PSUM is the TensorE landing buffer with read-accumulate-write per 4 B element controlled only by TensorE; VectorE/ScalarE see it as plain SRAM.
trigger: Trying to accumulate into PSUM from a vector op, or routing PSUM reads through GpSimd.
fix: Accumulate on TensorE via repeated nc_matmul into the same bank; evict with ScalarE/VectorE.
check_sketch: flag GpSimd-mapped instructions with PSUM operands; flag non-TensorE writes expecting accumulate semantics.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Near-memory accumulation in PSUM; nki/get-started/about/memory-hierarchy-overview.rst :: NeuronCore internal memory

rule: Put non-linear functions (exp, gelu, sqrt, sigmoid, ...) on ScalarE via nisa.activation and fold the preceding multiply/add into the same instruction.
why: ScalarE has hardware non-linear evaluation plus a pipelined multiply-add before func; all activation instructions cost the same regardless of scale/bias use.
trigger: Separate nl.multiply / nl.add / nl.exp chain on a tile.
fix: exp = nisa.activation(nl.exp, data, bias=bias_tile[128,1], scale=scale_tile_or_const)  # 3x faster than 3 ops
check_sketch: detect tensor_scalar(mul/add) immediately feeding an activation on the same tile; suggest fusion.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Scalar Engine - Pipelined Multiply-Add / Instruction Combination; nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #6

rule: Route two-input elementwise ops (tensor_tensor) to VectorE; ScalarE can read only one input tensor per instruction.
why: ScalarE lanes stream one source tensor; VectorE can stream two (cost ~2N cycles vs ~N for one input).
trigger: Attempting elementwise add/mul of two tiles on ScalarE.
fix: nisa.tensor_tensor(dst, data1, data2, op=nl.add) (VectorE); use activation(scale=vec,bias=vec) only when the second operand is per-partition.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Scalar Engine Performance Consideration; Vector Engine Cost Model

rule: Choose the PF-transpose engine by context: TensorE nc_transpose (128x128 via identity matmul, fastest) when TensorE is idle; VectorE nc_transpose for 32x32 blocks; DMA transpose when ScalarE/VectorE are the bottleneck; free-dim/free-dim transposes need only dma_copy or access patterns.
why: TensorE transposes occupy the highest-FLOPS engine and need PSUM eviction; VectorE reshape banks only transpose within 32 partitions; DMA transposes cost DMA bandwidth.
trigger: Any nc_transpose or layout change in the kernel.
fix: Pick engine= in nisa.nc_transpose, or nisa.dma_transpose, per the bottleneck engine in the profile.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Alternative Use Case; Cross-partition Data Movement; nki/get-started/about/indexing-overview.rst :: Case #2; nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: SBUF2SBUF DMA transpose

rule: Reserve GpSimd for work the other engines cannot express (iota, triangular/causal masks, custom C++ ops, software DGE) and read per-instruction costs from the ISA docs; there is no cycle rule of thumb.
why: GpSimd is eight programmable 512-bit processors, each wired to 16 SBUF partitions (proc0 -> partitions 0-15, ...), with 64 KB TCM each on trn1; performance depends on the hand-tuned kernel per instruction.
trigger: Mask generation, index generation, or ops with no VectorE/ScalarE lowering.
fix: nisa.iota / nisa.affine_select style ops on GpSimd; keep GpSimd free if the kernel relies on swdge gathers.

rule: On trn1/inf2 do not expect VectorE and GpSimd to overlap SBUF work, nor VectorE and ScalarE to overlap PSUM work; on trn2 both overlap (PSUM: only if on different banks).
why: NeuronCore-v2 serializes VectorE/GpSimd SBUF accesses and VectorE/ScalarE PSUM accesses (compiler-enforced). NeuronCore-v3 lifted both restrictions, with full parallel PSUM bandwidth as long as accesses do not hit the same PSUM bank.
trigger: Scheduling PSUM eviction on ScalarE while VectorE reduces PSUM, or GpSimd masks alongside VectorE on trn1.
fix: On trn2 place concurrent VectorE and ScalarE PSUM consumers on different banks (different 2 KiB/partition regions); on trn1 do not count on the overlap.
check_sketch: on trn2: flag concurrent VectorE+ScalarE ops reading the same PSUM bank.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Data Movement restrictions; nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: Data Movement Updates

rule: Keep VectorE tensor_copy/tensor_scalar operands in SBUF, in BF16/FP16, with a contiguous inner-most free dim to get the 4x Trainium2 performance mode (2x if one condition fails or one side is PSUM; tensor_tensor gets 2x with both inputs SBUF BF16/FP16).
why: NeuronCore-v3 VectorE auto-detects these conditions and uses a wider shared memory bus (with GpSimd) for 512 BF16 elements/cycle; computation still happens in FP32.
trigger: VectorE-bound kernel using FP32 intermediates or strided inner dims.
fix: Store intermediates as bf16, avoid inner stride != 1 on VectorE copies, evict PSUM with ScalarE if VectorE is the bottleneck.
check_sketch: for VectorE ops on trn2: score 4x if all(SBUF, bf16/fp16, inner_step==1), 2x partial, 1x otherwise.

rule: On Trainium3, load-balance tensor_scalar and tensor_copy between VectorE and ScalarE (both support the 2x BF16 mode) by setting the engine argument.
why: NeuronCore-v4 ScalarE natively supports those instructions at 256 BF16/FP16/FP8 elements per cycle.
trigger: One of VectorE/ScalarE is saturated on trn3.
fix: nisa.tensor_scalar(..., engine=nisa.engine.scalar) for part of the work.

rule: On Trainium3 compute softmax exponentials with nisa.exponential on VectorE (exp(src - max) with fused row-sum) instead of activation(exp) on ScalarE.
why: The VectorE fast-exponential instruction runs at 4x the throughput of ScalarE activation exp and fuses the max subtraction and accumulation.
trigger: Attention softmax on trn3 bound by ScalarE exp.
fix: nisa.exponential(dst, src, max_value=row_max[M,1], reduce_res=row_sum[M,1])
check_sketch: on trn3 flag activation(op=exp) feeding a tensor_reduce(add).

rule: Sum across partitions with a matmul against a ones vector on TensorE only when TensorE is otherwise idle; sum along the free dim with nisa.tensor_reduce on VectorE.
why: Partition-dim summation on TensorE uses a single PE column (1/128 of the array); VectorE reduces along the free dim at full lane parallelism.
trigger: Reduction direction mismatched with layout (e.g. RMSNorm sum).
fix: Pick the layout so the reduction axis is the free dim for VectorE, or use TensorE for the P-dim sum in norm/softmax kernels where TensorE has slack.

rule: Know that broadcast_to across partitions lowers to a TensorE matmul with a ones stationary (is_stationary_onezero=True) and costs TensorE time plus PSUM eviction.
why: Broadcasting a single-partition vector to M partitions is implemented as ones[1,M].T @ v on the systolic array.
trigger: Frequent per-tile broadcasts in a matmul-bound kernel.
fix: Pre-broadcast once and keep the result in SBUF, or restructure so the per-partition operand is used as activation scale/bias.
check_sketch: count broadcast_to calls inside hot loops.

rule: For arbitrary partition permutations or broadcasts within a 32-partition group, use nisa.nc_stream_shuffle on VectorE rather than a TensorE matmul.
why: Each VectorE Reshape Bank serves 32 partitions and accepts a 32-entry shuffle mask SM[i] = source partition (mod 32); e.g. 32 zeros broadcasts partition 0.
trigger: Partition shuffles confined to quadrants.
fix: nisa.nc_stream_shuffle(dst, src, shuffle_mask=[...32 ints...])

rule: Convert engine cycle costs to time with the per-generation clocks: trn2 TensorE 2.4 GHz, VectorE 0.96 GHz, ScalarE 1.2 GHz, GpSimd 1.2 GHz (trn1: 2.8/1.12/1.4/1.4; trn3: 2.4/1.2/1.2/1.2).
why: Each engine has its own sequencer and clock; ScalarE/VectorE process 128 elements per cycle (one per partition lane), TensorE 2x128 inputs per cycle (4x128 for fp8 on trn2, 8x128 MXFP8 on trn3).
trigger: Any cycle-based cost estimate.
fix: time = cycles / f_engine.

rule: Write kernels assuming Tensor, Vector, Scalar and GpSimd engines execute four independent in-order instruction streams synchronized only by compiler-inserted semaphores.
why: Each engine has its own sequencer (fetch/decode/issue, 32-bit scalar registers); data dependencies across engines become semaphore waits that show up as idle gaps.
trigger: Designing the per-engine instruction mix.
fix: Balance work so no single engine's stream is much longer than the others; keep cross-engine dependencies coarse-grained.
check_sketch: per-engine busy time from an instruction cost model; report max/min imbalance.

rule: Let DMA triggers go through the Sync Engine (SP) when you do not want them to perturb compute-engine instruction ordering.
why: The Sync Engine is a sequencer that executes control instructions (semaphore waits, DMA triggers) without a data path.
trigger: DMA triggers interleaved into a saturated ScalarE stream.
fix: nisa.dma_copy(..., dge_mode=hwdge, engine=nisa.engine.sync)

rule: Fill all 128 partitions in every VectorE/ScalarE/GpSimd instruction; an instruction using 32 lanes costs the same as one using 128.
why: Each partition maps one-to-one to a vector lane; cost scales with free-dim length, not lane count.
trigger: Instruction operand channels=64 (or less) in the profiler.
fix: Partition-vectorize: place independent small tiles in disjoint partition ranges and process with one instruction.
check_sketch: flag compute ops with P < 128 inside hot loops.

rule: Put the contraction dim K on the partition axis of both matmul inputs: nc_matmul(stationary[K,M], moving[K,N]) computes stationary.T @ moving -> [M,N].
why: Each SBUF partition feeds one row of PEs, so K is streamed across partitions; the free axis of stationary becomes the output partition axis and the free axis of moving becomes the output free axis.
trigger: Any matmul formulation.
fix: Deliver LHS pre-transposed ([K,M]) from the framework when possible to avoid an on-chip transpose.
check_sketch: assert stationary.shape[0]==moving.shape[0]<=128.

rule: Respect nc_matmul limits: stationary free <= 128, partition (K) <= 128, moving free <= 512 (one PSUM bank = 512 fp32 per partition).
why: 128 PE columns bound stationary_fsize; 128 PE rows/SBUF partitions bound K; each instruction writes a single PSUM bank holding 512 fp32 values per partition.
trigger: Shapes exceeding these in a single call.
fix: Tile M and N into independent calls; tile K into accumulating calls into the same PSUM tile.
check_sketch: check against nl.tile_size.gemm_stationary_fmax=128, pmax=128, gemm_moving_fmax=512, psum_bank_fmax=512.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Tile Size; nki/get-started/about/tiling-overview.rst :: Tile size considerations

rule: Aim for long runs of LoadStationary(128x128) / MultiplyMoving(128x512) pairs with no intervening engine switches.
why: TensorE is deeply pipelined with background LoadStationary; the largest tiles keep the array in the regime where MM, not LS, bounds throughput.
trigger: Matmul-heavy kernels with TensorE < 90% busy or small MM free sizes.
fix: Reorder loops so the moving tile reaches N=512 and the stationary tile is reused across several moving tiles.
check_sketch: compute avg moving free size and stationary reuse count per nc_matmul.

rule: Estimate MultiplyMoving cost as max(N, 64) TensorE cycles for BF16/FP16/TF32/FP8 inputs (N = moving free size); FP32 inputs cost ~4x.
why: TensorE is pipelined so initiation interval, not latency, matters; MM_INIT_LATENCY is 64 cycles on NeuronCore-v2 and small-N instructions are turnaround-bound.
trigger: Cost modeling or many small-N matmuls.
fix: Downcast FP32 operands to BF16/FP16/TF32/FP8 before matmul; keep N >= 64 (ideally 512).
check_sketch: mm_cycles = max(N, 64) * (4 if fp32 else 1).

rule: For matrix-vector products (decode GEMV, M or N << 128), make the large matrix the stationary tensor and the short vector the moving tensor.
why: LoadStationary is pure data movement and runs up to 4x faster than a MultiplyMoving of the same free size; with the short tensor as moving, MM issues every ~64 cycles instead of every ~128+.
trigger: Profiler shows LDWEIGHTS with 1 element/partition and MATMUL with 128 elements/partition, or nl.matmul with a [1,K] x [K,N] shape.
fix: Swap operands: nc_matmul(stationary=W[K,128], moving=x[K,1..]) and transpose the (tiny) output, or restructure to batch tokens into N.
check_sketch: flag nc_matmul where stationary free size < moving free size / 4 and stationary free < 32.

rule: Use TensorE peak numbers per NeuronCore-v3 for roofline math: 158 FP8, 79 BF16/FP16/TF32, 20 FP32 dense TFLOPS (316 sparse); 8 cores give 1299 FP8 / 667 BF16 / 181 FP32 TFLOPS per chip.
why: TensorE is a 128x128 systolic array at 2.4 GHz with 2x128 inputs/cycle (4x128 FP8).
trigger: Computing ridge point: 79e12 FLOPS / (2.9e12/8 B/s per core) ~ 218 FLOP/B per core for BF16.
fix: If arithmetic intensity (FLOP per HBM byte) < ~218 on trn2 BF16 the kernel is memory-bound; optimize DMA, not TensorE.
check_sketch: ai = flops / hbm_bytes; compare to 79e12 / 362e9.

rule: To double matmul throughput on Trainium2, use FP8_E4/FP8_E5 inputs with perf_mode=nisa.matmul_perf_mode.double_row and shapes stationary [128,2,128], moving [128,2,512] (K=256 per instruction).
why: Each PE multiplies two FP8 pairs per cycle; the contraction dim 256 is split into 128 partitions x a major free dim of 2. The sequence takes the same time as a BF16 K=128 pair. FP8_E3 gets no speedup. Accumulation remains FP32.
trigger: FP8-quantized weights on trn2 with K >= 256.
fix: Pad K to a multiple of 2 with zeros; do not combine with column tiling, sparse matmul, or transpose mode; mixing E4 in one operand and E5 in the other is allowed.
check_sketch: if dtype in (fp8_e4, fp8_e5) and perf_mode==double_row: assert shape[1]==2 for both operands.

rule: On Trainium2 use nisa.nc_transpose(engine=tensor) / nc_matmul(is_transpose=True) rather than an explicit identity matmul.
why: Transpose mode is bit-accurate for NaN/Inf, 2x faster for FP32, and emits FP16/BF16 PSUM output for 16-bit inputs (halving eviction bytes) instead of FP32. FP8 input yields 16-bit output with upper 8 bits zero.
trigger: Any PF transpose on trn2.
fix: nisa.nc_transpose(dst, src, engine=nisa.engine.tensor)
check_sketch: flag nc_matmul whose moving/stationary is a constant identity.

rule: Accumulate over K > 128 by issuing successive nc_matmul calls into the same PSUM tile; the first write overwrites and later ones accumulate in FP32 (auto-detected, or set accumulate=True/False).
why: PSUM supports read-accumulate-write per element driven by TensorE; a run of matmuls into one bank is a matmul accumulation group.
trigger: K-tiled matmuls.
fix: psum = nl.ndarray((M,N), fp32, buffer=nl.psum); for k in range(K//128): nisa.nc_matmul(dst=psum, stationary=a[k], moving=b[k])
check_sketch: verify all K-slices target the same PSUM allocation and no intervening non-TensorE write.

rule: Rotate output tiles across the 8 PSUM banks (8 x 2 KiB per partition) so TensorE can start the next accumulation group while VectorE/ScalarE evict the previous one.
why: PSUM has 128 partitions x 16 KiB = 8 banks of 512 fp32; TensorE can have up to eight outstanding accumulation groups.
trigger: TensorE idle waiting for PSUM eviction (semaphore on Vector/Scalar).
fix: Allocate PSUM result tiles per (m,n) tile inside the loop so the allocator double/triple-buffers banks.
check_sketch: count live PSUM tiles; flag if 1 bank reused serially with eviction on the critical path.

rule: Make the stationary free size 128 so MATMUL uses all 128 PE columns; a '128*96' operand in the profiler means 25% of the array is idle.
why: The stationary free axis maps to PE columns / output partitions; fewer than 128 leaves columns unused at the same instruction cost.
trigger: MATMUL instruction operand field showing < 128 output partitions.
fix: Partition-vectorize: write two 64-row outputs into partitions 0-63 and 64-127 of one PSUM tile and process them with one downstream instruction.
check_sketch: flag nc_matmul with stationary free size < 128 in hot loops.

rule: Choose which operand is stationary based on the layout the consumer needs: output is [stationary_free, moving_free], so swapping operands yields the transposed output for free.
why: nc_matmul(moving, stationary) = (stationary.T @ moving).T; e.g. linear -> layernorm needs features on the free dim for bn_stats, so put the input feature map as stationary.
trigger: A PF transpose between a matmul and its consumer (bn_stats, tensor_reduce, next matmul).
fix: Swap stationary/moving in nisa.nc_matmul; for RMSNorm keep weight stationary and do the cross-partition sum on TensorE.
check_sketch: detect nc_transpose on a matmul output; propose operand swap.

rule: When TensorE looks saturated, color the Device Timeline by tensor_instruction_type and measure how much is Transpose vs Regular before optimizing matmuls.
why: Transposes are 'not useful' TensorE work; a large red share means layout fixes (IO layout, operand swap, alternative engine) beat matmul tuning.
trigger: TensorE > 90% busy but MFU low.
fix: Reduce IO transposes by choosing kernel IO layout; reduce intermediate transposes by operand swap or engine choice.

rule: On Trainium3 use nisa.nc_matmul_mx with x4-packed MXFP8/MXFP4 tiles (stationary [128,128], moving [128,512] in _x4 types = K of 512) plus uint8 scale tiles for 4x BF16 throughput.
why: Each PE does four MX multiply-accumulates per cycle; K=512 is split as 128 partitions x 4 packed elements that were 128 apart in the original contraction axis; scales (group of 32 = 8 partitions x 4 elements) live in the same SBUF quadrant as their data, 4 partitions per quadrant.
trigger: Quantized MLP/attention projections on trn3.
fix: Interleave data with a strided tensor_copy or DMA, quantize with nisa.quantize_mx on VectorE (src must be SBUF; no FP4 output), call nc_matmul_mx(dst, stationary, moving, stationary_scale, moving_scale) with BF16 or FP32 PSUM dst.
check_sketch: check _x4 dtype shapes and scale tile shapes ([P, F//4] uint8, oversized when P>32).

rule: On Trainium3 write matmul results directly as BF16 into PSUM (and accumulate into BF16 PSUM) to halve eviction bytes, choosing RNE or stochastic rounding.
why: NeuronCore-v4 downcasts FP32 array output immediately before the PSUM write; accumulation into a BF16 PSUM tensor upcasts, adds in FP32, and rounds back.
trigger: Memory/eviction-bound matmul chains on trn3 that tolerate bf16 partial sums.
fix: Allocate the PSUM dst with dtype=nl.bfloat16.

rule: On Trainium3, matmuls with small contraction (packed K <= 64, i.e. unquantized K <= 256 for MX) can be PE row-tiled to run in parallel on TensorE.
why: Matmul-MX supports row-tiling only; with the 4x effective K this covers more shapes.
trigger: Many small-K MX matmuls.
fix: Group small-K matmuls so the hardware/compiler can row-tile them.

rule: Consider M:N structured-sparse weights on Trainium2/3 for up to 4x TensorE throughput (316 TFLOPS on trn2); the NKI sparse_matmul API was not yet published in these docs.
why: TensorE rows can read from 4/2/1 SBUF partitions per compression ratio; supported patterns 4:16, 4:12, 4:8, 2:8, 2:4, 1:4, 1:2 with a packed uint16 tag tensor.
trigger: Weight matrices that can be pruned to 4:8 or sparser.
fix: Prepare compressed stationary [128,128] + tags [128,32] uint16 and moving [128, CR, 512] when the API ships.

rule: Pay the MX interleave (elements 128 apart packed into quads) offline for weights and fold it into an existing strided VectorE/ScalarE pass for activations; DMA strided interleave is much slower.
why: Quantize-MX preserves layout, so the interleaved layout must exist before quantization; on-device TensorCopy with strided access is the fast path, DMA strided access only makes sense when fully hidden behind compute.
trigger: Preparing MXFP8 inputs on trn3.
fix: Reshape BF16 [512,512] as [4,128,512] and copy with a strided access pattern into [128, 512, 4], then quantize_mx.

rule: Plan SBUF residency against 28 MiB on Trainium2 (128 partitions x 224 KiB), 24 MiB on trn1 (192 KiB/partition), 32 MiB on trn3; PSUM is 2 MiB (16 KiB/partition, 8 banks of 2 KiB) on all generations.
why: SBUF/PSUM are software-managed 2-D SRAMs; exceeding capacity triggers compiler spills to HBM.
trigger: Choosing block sizes / number of resident weight tiles.
fix: Keep live tiles well below 224 KiB per partition on trn2 (e.g. a [128, 4096] bf16 tile is 8 KiB/partition).
check_sketch: sum bytes per partition of simultaneously live SBUF tiles; flag > 90% of 224 KiB.

rule: Allocate tiles so their start partition obeys the hardware rule: >64 partitions start at 0; 33-64 start at 0 or 64; <=32 start at 0/32/64/96.
why: The engine read/write interfaces are organized in 32-partition quadrants and 64-partition halves; the compiler allocator enforces this, so odd sizes waste partitions.
trigger: Tiles of 48, 96 or 100 partitions, or partition-vectorization placing a second tile at partition 40.
fix: Use partition counts of 32/64/128 and place sub-tiles at 0/32/64/96.
check_sketch: for explicit partition slices: assert start in allowed set for size.

rule: Never stride along the partition dimension in one instruction access; the leading access-pattern step must equal the tensor's full free-dim element count.
why: Hardware reads a contiguous block of partitions with the same free-dim offset per time step.
trigger: t.ap(pattern=[[2*F, P/2], ...]) or t[::2, :] on SBUF/PSUM tensors.
fix: Use nc_stream_shuffle / transposes to rearrange partitions, or restructure the layout.
check_sketch: for SBUF/PSUM .ap(): assert pattern[0][0] == prod(free_shape).

rule: Keep the most-minor free-dim stride at or below 16 bytes (4 fp32, 8 bf16, 16 fp8 elements) on SBUF/PSUM accesses; larger strides halve the engine's read/write bandwidth (~50% slower instruction).
why: Each tensor read/write interface delivers 128 elements/cycle only when the inner stride is < 16 B.
trigger: Strided inner access such as x[:, ::8] in bf16 (16 B stride) or even/odd column splits in fp32 with stride > 4.
fix: Reorder dims so the strided axis is not the innermost, or copy once into a contiguous layout.
check_sketch: for compute ops: inner_step*dtype_bytes > 16 -> warn 2x slowdown.

rule: Amortize the ~60-cycle fixed cost of each tensor access request with large P and F sizes.
why: Initiating a read/write stream between an engine and SBUF/PSUM costs about 60 cycles on NeuronCore-v2; ILP hides some but small tiles expose it.
trigger: Many instructions on tiles with few elements per partition.
fix: Batch work into fewer instructions with >= 128 elements per partition.
check_sketch: per instruction cost += 60 cycles.

rule: Keep instruction free sizes within 64K elements for SBUF operands and 4K elements for PSUM operands (bn_stats: <= 512), and remember each free axis is a uint16 size with int16 stride.
why: ISA encodes up to four free dims per partition with 16-bit size/stride fields; most instructions only support 1-3 dims.
trigger: Very long single-instruction tiles.
fix: Split into multiple instructions or add an outer loop.
check_sketch: assert each free size <= 65535, PSUM free <= 4096, bn_stats free <= 512.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Vector Engine Layout & Tile Size; Accessing SBUF/PSUM tensors

rule: Reserve PSUM for TensorE outputs and evict results to SBUF with VectorE/ScalarE as soon as each accumulation group completes.
why: PSUM is only 2 MiB; holding results there blocks TensorE from reusing banks and VectorE/ScalarE can only treat it as plain SRAM.
trigger: Vector/scalar intermediates allocated in PSUM, or late eviction.
fix: tensor_copy/activation from PSUM -> SBUF immediately after the K loop; do not allocate non-matmul tensors in nl.psum.
check_sketch: flag nl.ndarray(buffer=nl.psum) not written by nc_matmul.

rule: Expect no cross-partition data movement for instructions spanning > 64 partitions; 33-64 partitions allow cross-half moves and <= 32 allow cross-quadrant moves (one-to-one mapping only).
why: src and dst must occupy the same partition count, and start-partition rules force both to start at 0 when > 64; smaller tiles may map half-to-half or quadrant-to-quadrant.
trigger: Trying to shift data across partitions with a tensor_copy on a 128-partition tile.
fix: Use 32- or 64-partition sub-tiles for quadrant/half moves, VectorE 32x32 transpose/shuffle, TensorE matmul-based reshapes, or DMA SBUF->SBUF.
check_sketch: flag copy ops whose src and dst partition offsets differ while P > 64.

rule: Declare per-iteration SBUF buffers inside the innermost loop rather than as one large outer array indexed by loop variables.
why: A big outer allocation (e.g. (2,4,par_dim(128),512)) stays live across the whole nest and can cause unexpected spilling; per-iteration declarations let the compiler recycle space.
trigger: Spill traffic appears although the working set seemed small.
fix: for i0: for i1: buf = nl.ndarray((nl.par_dim(128), 512), buffer=nl.sbuf); buf[...] = nl.load(...)
check_sketch: flag multi-dimensional SBUF allocations indexed by loop vars with leading non-partition dims.

rule: Inside nl.dynamic_range bodies keep the number and size of live tiles small; everything live stays resident in SBUF/PSUM for the entire loop.
why: The hardware re-executes one body copy, so tensors allocated in the body are allocated once and reused; the compiler cannot stagger allocations across iterations.
trigger: Large working sets in a dynamic loop causing allocation failure or spills.
fix: Hoist constants out, reuse buffers explicitly, reduce block size in dynamic loops.
check_sketch: sum live bytes/partition in dynamic_range body vs 224 KiB.

rule: If Spill Save Bytes exceeds ~30% of Sbuf Read Bytes (or Spill Reload Bytes ~30% of Sbuf Write Bytes) in the Summary tab, fuse operators or shrink blocks.
why: The compiler spills intermediates to a TMPBUF in HBM and reloads them via qSyncSpillReload queues when SBUF overflows; this traffic competes with useful DMA.
trigger: Summary data_movement metrics; instructions waiting on qSyncSpillReload.
fix: Loop-fuse producer/consumer so each tile goes load -> op0 -> op1 -> store; reduce oversized blocks.

rule: Lay out every SBUF/PSUM tile as a rectangle: same free-dim start offset on every partition it spans.
why: Tensors are described by a partition offset/size and a byte offset/size within each partition; an SBUF [128,64] bf16 tile at byte offset 1024 occupies bytes 1024-1151 in each partition.
trigger: Hand allocation with per-partition offsets.
fix: Use nl.ndarray or direct allocation with a single (partition, byte) rectangle.

rule: On Trainium3 pack MX scale tiles from up to four quantized tensors into one [128, F//4] uint8 allocation at partition offsets 0/4/8/12 within each quadrant.
why: Scales must sit in the same 32-partition quadrant as their data; only 4 of 32 partitions per quadrant are used by one tensor, so oversized scale tiles waste 28/32 of their space unless packed.
trigger: Several quantize_mx outputs each allocating a full oversized scale tile.
fix: Slice the scale tile per quadrant offset when calling quantize_mx / nc_matmul_mx.

rule: Loop over the leading tensor dimension in chunks of nl.tile_size.pmax (128); any tile with partition size > 128 fails to compile.
why: SBUF and PSUM have 128 partitions and every tile maps shape[0] to the partition dimension.
trigger: Error 'Size of partition dimension 256 exceeds architecture limitation of 128'.
fix: for p in range(ceil(P/128)): slice p*128:min((p+1)*128, P) and handle the ragged tail with min().
check_sketch: assert tile.shape[0] <= 128.

rule: Give every ScalarE/VectorE instruction at least ~128 elements per partition; one-element instructions run at ~100x overhead.
why: Static instruction overhead is ~100 engine cycles; dependent one-element tensor_scalar chains measured 222 ns (266 ScalarE cycles on NC-v3) initiation interval versus 1 cycle of useful work.
trigger: Profiler access pattern like fp32@0x4000[1,1,1][1,1,1] repeated back-to-back with src==previous dst.
fix: Reformulate (e.g. Mamba prefix scan with nisa.tensor_tensor_scan instead of seq_len tensor_scalars) so each instruction covers a long free dim.
check_sketch: flag compute ops with free size < 128 in loops with trip count > 16.
source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #5a; nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Vector Engine Cost Model

rule: Merge several < 128-partition instructions of the same op into one 128-partition instruction by placing their inputs in disjoint partition ranges.
why: Instruction cost is independent of lane count, so two 64-partition reductions serialized cost 2x a single 128-partition one.
trigger: channels=64 (or smaller) operands repeated back-to-back.
fix: mm_tile = nl.zeros((128, ...), buffer=nl.psum); mm_tile[0:64] = nc_matmul(...); mm_tile[64:128] = nc_matmul(...); reduce = nisa.tensor_reduce(mm_tile, ...)
check_sketch: group consecutive same-op instructions with P<=64 whose partition ranges can be stacked.

rule: Pick instruction tile sizes large enough to amortize ~100-cycle overhead but small enough to pipeline across engines and fit SBUF; iterate with the profiler.
why: Too small exposes instruction overhead; too large delays downstream engines (long first-tile latency) and raises SBUF pressure (spills).
trigger: Engine idle gaps at pipeline start, or spills, after enlarging tiles.
fix: Start at 128x512 per instruction; grow the free dim only while engine utilization improves.

rule: When K is blocked beyond what PSUM can hold, accumulate partial results in an SBUF fp32 tile with nisa.tensor_tensor(op=add) and store coalesced [128, BLOCK_N] rows.
why: The tutorial's final kernel (TILES_IN_BLOCK_M=16, N=2, K=8) turned a DMA-bound matmul (DMA 99.9% / TensorE 87%) into a compute-bound one (DMA 21.5% / TensorE 99.5% / VectorE 10.6%).
trigger: Matmul kernel with DMA active near 100% and TensorE < 90%.
fix: Load [TILE_K, BLOCK_N] and [TILE_K, BLOCK_M] blocks per K-block; memset fp32 result tiles; add PSUM into them; pack and store per N-block.
