rule: Load each input tile once per outer iteration (hoist loads to the outer loop) instead of reloading inside the innermost loop.
why: In the naive loop the m=0,k=0 tile is reloaded N/TILE_N times; the Tensor Info widget's Load to SBUF Repeat Factor quantifies this (e.g. 16).
trigger: Repeat factor >> 1 for a tensor in the Tensor Info widget.
fix: Build lists of SBUF tiles for a row/column block in the outer loop, then reuse across the inner loop; trade against SBUF capacity.
check_sketch: count distinct dma loads of the same HBM region per kernel.

rule: Assert kernel input shapes match the tiling the kernel implements; mismatched larger inputs silently produce garbage for untouched regions.
why: There is no bounds checking: a [128,512] kernel applied to a [256,512] tensor leaves the bottom half uninitialized.
trigger: Output rows beyond the processed tile contain random values.
fix: assert in_tensor.shape == (X, Y) or loop over ceil(P/128).
check_sketch: compare kernel loop coverage with declared input shapes.

rule: Slice multi-engine operator chains into tiles so ScalarE, VectorE, TensorE and GpSimd process different tiles concurrently (e.g. attention: matmuls on TensorE, exp on ScalarE, sum on VectorE, rescale on ScalarE, causal mask on GpSimd).
why: Without tiling, each engine waits for the previous engine to finish the whole tensor; with tiling the first tile unblocks the next engine early.
trigger: Idle-gap first instruction waits on a semaphore named after another engine (e.g. S[4] (Scalar) == 6).
fix: Restructure loops so each iteration emits a tile's worth of work for every engine.

rule: Issue loads for tile i+1 (or block i+1) before computing tile i so DMA runs in parallel with compute.
why: DMA engines are asynchronous; the compiler overlaps independent loads if dependencies and SBUF space allow. Idle gaps whose wait is on a q* semaphore (qSyncIO0) mean compute is blocked on loads.
trigger: EVENT_SEMAPHORE waiting on S[32] (qSyncIO0) before compute instructions.
fix: Allocate double buffers for input tiles and hoist the next load above the current compute in program order.

rule: Avoid long chains where every instruction consumes the previous instruction's output tile with tiny free sizes; add ~100 engine cycles per instruction in that regime.
why: A RAW dependency forces the next instruction to wait until the previous output is fully committed to SRAM, exposing static overhead instead of pipelining.
trigger: src address of inst_i equals dst of inst_{i-1} across many consecutive instructions.
fix: Batch independent rows into one instruction, or use scan/fused instructions.
check_sketch: detect chains of length > 8 with free size < 128 where each op reads the previous op's dst.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Vector Engine Cost Model; nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #5a

rule: Combine multiply + add + nonlinearity (activation), activation + free-dim sum (activation_reduce), and scans (tensor_tensor_scan) into single ISA instructions on VectorE/ScalarE-bound kernels.
why: Deep engine pipelines perform the extra ops at no additional cost; ActReadAccumulator costs only ~64 ScalarE cycles to dump the reduction.
trigger: Profile where VectorE or ScalarE is busy at all times while TensorE idles (self-attention inner loop).
fix: nisa.activation_reduce(op=nl.exp, data, bias, scale, reduce_op=nl.add, reduce_res=row_sum)
check_sketch: pattern-match activation followed by tensor_reduce(add) over the same tile.

rule: Use nl.dynamic_range for trip counts unknown at compile time or large enough that unrolling bloats compile time/code size; keep range() for everything else.
why: range()/static_range/affine_range/sequential_range fully unroll at specialization; dynamic_range emits one hardware loop instruction whose step must be a compile-time positive int and whose loop variable is a device register (cannot be used in host-side if).
trigger: Compile time explodes or code size scales with sequence length.
fix: for i in nl.dynamic_range(start_reg, stop_reg, 128): ... using .ap(scalar_offset=i) for addressing.
check_sketch: flag unrolled loops with trip count > ~256 containing DMAs.
source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dynamic-loops.rst :: Comparison with Other Range Iterators; When to Use dynamic_range

rule: Place nl.no_reorder() blocks inside a dynamic_range body, never around the dynamic loop.
why: dynamic_range loops inside no_reorder are unsupported and error; the reverse nesting is allowed.
trigger: with nl.no_reorder(): for i in nl.dynamic_range(n): ...
fix: for i in nl.dynamic_range(n): with nl.no_reorder(): ...
check_sketch: AST check for dynamic_range nested in no_reorder.

rule: Make each pipeline stage's tile large enough that its compute exceeds the ~1.3 us cross-engine semaphore round trip; do not synchronize engines per tiny tile.
why: Semaphore-to-start latency is about 1300 ns cross-engine, so fine-grained handoffs leave engines waiting more than working.
trigger: Many short instructions separated by semaphore waits in the trace.
fix: Coarsen tiles (e.g. 128 x 512+ elements per stage) so each stage runs >= several microseconds.
check_sketch: per stage: compute_time vs 1300 ns; flag stages shorter than ~2x.
source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dma-bandwidth-guide.rst :: Why Large Contiguous DMA Payloads Are Required

rule: Order TensorE work so the next LoadStationary overlaps the current MultiplyMoving; whichever of LS or MM reads the longer tensor bounds throughput.
why: TensorE supports background LoadStationary; with stationary 128x128 and moving 128x512 the engine is MM-bound (case a), the desired regime.
trigger: TensorE utilization limited by LS (short moving tensors).
fix: Reuse one stationary across several moving tiles; prefer long moving free dims.
check_sketch: tensore_time = sum(max(LS_cost, MM_cost)) per pair.

rule: On trn3 expect Quantize-MX (VectorE) to consume matmul output at half the rate TensorE produces it; rely on tiled reuse of quantized tiles rather than back-to-back matmul -> quantize -> matmul on small tensors.
why: TensorE runs at double the VectorE clock; back-pressure only appears for small tensors where no reuse hides the quantization.
trigger: Small-tensor MX chains stalling TensorE.
fix: Increase tile reuse or interleave independent matmuls.

rule: Write kernels in natural sequential order and let the compiler reorder independent operations; the NKI compiler preserves your explicit allocation and scheduling choices.
why: NKI is a sequential programming model; independent ops are reordered for performance, dependent ones are synchronized across engines automatically.
trigger: Over-constraining with no_reorder or manual semaphores.
fix: Use nl.no_reorder only to pin a critical pipeline order.
source: nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Core Programming Model; nki/deep-dives/nki-compiler.rst :: Overview

rule: Launch on both physical cores of a Trainium2/3 logical core with kernel[2](...) and split work by nl.program_id(0) in {0,1}; nl.num_programs() reports the count.
why: An LNC can contain up to two physical NeuronCores sharing HBM; each receives its own program_id.
trigger: Any kernel whose work divides into two independent halves.
fix: i = nl.program_id(0); process input[i]; kernel[8] errors on current hardware.
check_sketch: check kernel is launched with [2] when num_programs branches exist.
source: nki/get-started/about/lnc.rst :: Launching a kernel on multiple cores; nki/nki_faq.rst

rule: Allocate LNC kernel inputs/outputs in nl.shared_hbm so both cores can address them.
why: The two physical cores of an LNC share one HBM address space; private buffers are not visible across cores.
trigger: Output allocated with buffer=nl.hbm in an LNC=2 kernel.
fix: out = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm)
check_sketch: flag kernel outputs not in shared_hbm when launched with [2].

rule: Keep dynamic control flow identical on both cores of an LNC; divergent device-side branches are undefined behavior (likely runtime error).
why: The SDK assumes each core runs 'the same' program; static (compile-time) branches on program_id are fine, dynamic register-based divergence is not.
trigger: while reg: loops whose condition differs per core.
fix: Make trip counts/conditions core-independent or pad work so both cores execute the same dynamic path.
check_sketch: flag dynamic_range/while conditions derived from program_id-dependent data.

rule: For memory-bound (decode) kernels under LNC=2, split the HBM streaming across both physical cores so both sets of 16 DMA engines pull from the shared HBM bank.
why: Trainium2 has 4 HBM banks of 24 GB, each shared by two physical cores; chip HBM bandwidth 2.9-3 TB/s over 8 cores is ~360-375 GB/s per core, matching one core's 16-engine DMA peak of 368 GB/s. A single core therefore cannot use the bank's full bandwidth; two cores can approach ~2x.
trigger: LNC=2 kernel where program_id 1 does little while program_id 0 streams weights.
fix: Shard weight rows/heads by program_id so each core DMAs half the bytes; each core still needs >= 4 KiB/partition transfers.
check_sketch: in [2]-launched kernels compare DMA bytes issued under each program_id branch.

rule: Compile with --lnc (or --logical-nc-config) equal to the runtime NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG; only 1 or 2 are valid and 2 is the trn2 default.
why: The compiler shards the graph for the LNC degree; a mismatch with the runtime grouping is unsupported.
trigger: Kernel tested with NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=1 but compiled with -lnc 2.
fix: torch_neuronx.trace(..., compiler_args='--lnc=1') with os.environ['NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG']='1'.

rule: Exchange data between the two cores of an LNC through shared HBM / local collectives instead of the NeuronLink network.
why: Under LNC=2 the cores share an address space and can perform local collective operations without network traffic.
trigger: Reductions across the two halves of an LNC-sharded kernel.
fix: Write partials to shared_hbm, nisa.core_barrier(data, cores), then reduce.

rule: Overlap collectives with compute: dedicated CC-Cores and NeuronLink handle AllReduce/ReduceScatter/AllGather/All2all while engines keep computing.
why: Trainium2 has 16-20 CC-Cores (docs disagree: 20 in the NKI guide, 16 on the hardware page) and 4 NeuronLink-v3 at 1.28 TB/s per chip (1024 GB/s intra-instance, 256 GB/s inter-instance in an UltraServer).
trigger: Tensor-parallel decode where all-reduce latency is exposed.
fix: Issue the collective (nisa.sendrecv / core_barrier or framework CC) early and keep independent compute after it.

rule: On Trainium3 UltraServers design MoE/all-to-all style communication around the switched all-to-all fabric: 256 GB/s intra-server, 320 GB/s inter-server, 128 GB/s inter-rack per chip.
why: NeuronSwitch-v1 PCIe Gen6 fabric replaces the 2D torus; routing is address-based and transparent, with semaphore writes following the data path.
trigger: Expert-parallel dispatch on trn3.
fix: Keep per-chip all-to-all volume within these link budgets; prefer intra-server placement for the heaviest pairs.

rule: Use nisa.core_barrier(data, cores) and nisa.sendrecv(src, dst, send_to_rank, recv_from_rank, pipe_id) for intra-kernel multi-core coordination.
why: NKI exposes collective primitives so kernels can synchronize and exchange data across NeuronCores without leaving the kernel.
trigger: Multi-core NKI kernels needing a barrier or point-to-point exchange.
fix: Call core_barrier before reading another core's shared_hbm output.
source: nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Direct Hardware Control with nki.isa

rule: Rely on FP32 accumulation inside TensorE/PSUM regardless of input dtype; before Trainium3 the matmul output in PSUM is always FP32 (except transpose mode).
why: The systolic array accumulates in FP32 and PSUM near-memory accumulation is FP32; trn3 adds optional BF16 PSUM output with rounding at the write.
trigger: Allocating a bf16 PSUM dst on trn1/trn2.
fix: psum = nl.ndarray((M,N), nl.float32, buffer=nl.psum); downcast during eviction (tensor_copy to bf16 SBUF).
check_sketch: on trn1/trn2 assert nc_matmul dst dtype is fp32 unless is_transpose.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Tensor Engine Data Types; nki/guides/architecture/trainium3_arch.rst :: BF16 Matmul Results in PSUM

rule: Downcast FP32 matmul operands to BF16/FP16/TF32 (or FP8) before nc_matmul; FP32 inputs run ~4x slower (20 vs 79 TFLOPS on trn2).
why: TensorE processes 16-bit inputs at 2x128 elements/cycle; FP32 takes multiple passes.
trigger: nc_matmul with fp32 stationary/moving.
fix: Cast during load/eviction (tensor_copy dtype=nl.bfloat16) and keep weights in bf16 in HBM.
check_sketch: flag nc_matmul operands with dtype float32.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Tensor Engine Cost Model; nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: Tensor Engine

rule: Store VectorE/ScalarE intermediates in bf16 freely: arithmetic is always FP32 internally with zero-overhead input/output casting, so low-precision storage costs no accuracy inside the instruction.
why: VectorE/ScalarE lanes cast to/from FP32 at no throughput cost; trn2 performance mode is enabled by bf16/fp16 operands without changing precision.
trigger: Keeping fp32 tiles 'for accuracy' on the vector path.
fix: Use bf16 SBUF tiles between instructions, fp32 only for running accumulators that need it.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Vector Engine / Scalar Engine Data Types; nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: Vector Engine Performance Mode

rule: Choose FP8 formats deliberately: FP8_E5M2 (5-bit exp), FP8_E4M3 (4-bit exp), FP8_E3M4; cFP8 on trn2 has adjustable exponent bias, and only E4/E5 get the double-rate matmul.
why: NeuronCore-v2/v3 support configurable FP8; E3M4 matmuls run at BF16 speed.
trigger: Selecting a quantization format for weights/activations.
fix: Use E4M3 for weights/activations needing precision and E5M2 for range; avoid E3M4 for performance paths.
check_sketch: flag matmul inputs of fp8_e3m4 when perf is the goal.
source: about-neuron/arch/neuron-features/data-types.rst :: Trn1 / Inf2 (NeuronCore v2); about-neuron/arch/neuron-hardware/neuron-core-v3.rst :: Tensor Engine; nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: Double FP8

rule: Pick the rounding mode explicitly: RNE is the hardware default; enable stochastic rounding with NEURON_RT_STOCHASTIC_ROUNDING_EN=1 (default on in PyTorch-Neuron when XLA_USE_BF16=1) when accumulating small increments into bf16/fp16.
why: RNE squashes small addends into large values (1024 + 0.5 x 2048 stays 1024 in fp16); SR rounds probabilistically so increments accumulate (result ~2056). Available since NeuronCore-v2.
trigger: Low-precision running sums, optimizer updates, long accumulation chains.
fix: Set the env var at runtime; on trn3 choose RNE or SR for BF16 PSUM downcasts.
source: about-neuron/arch/neuron-features/rounding-modes.rst :: Stochastic Rounding (SR) / Quick Tests; about-neuron/arch/neuron-features/data-types.rst :: Rounding Modes

rule: Do not transpose tensors that may contain NaN/Inf with an identity matmul on trn1; the NaN/Inf propagates across the output. Use trn2+ transpose mode (is_transpose=True) for bit-accurate transposes.
why: Matmul-based transpose multiplies by 0.0/1.0 and accumulates, so NaN*0 = NaN spreads along the accumulation chain.
trigger: Transposing logits/attention scores with masked -inf values on trn1.
fix: Mask after transposing, or use DMA transpose / VectorE 32x32 transpose which are bit-accurate.
check_sketch: flag TensorE transposes of tiles produced after a -inf mask on trn1.

rule: Expect integer matmul, all-reduce, reduce-scatter and scatter-with-compute to be auto-converted to FP32, and 64-bit ints to 32-bit unless --native-int64 (trn2+).
why: These ops lack a native integer datapath; --implicit-integer-downcast controls whether the conversion warns or errors.
trigger: Index arithmetic in int64 or integer matmuls.
fix: Use int32 indices; compute index math on GpSimd (native 16x int32 per processor) or VectorE.
check_sketch: flag int64 tensors and integer-typed nc_matmul.

rule: Use GpSimd for genuinely integer/low-precision SIMD work: each processor natively does 16x FP32/INT32, 32x FP16/INT16 or 64x INT8 per cycle (VectorE/ScalarE compute only in FP32).
why: GpSimd is a 512-bit vector machine per processor; it can also cast to/from FP32 at no cost when reading SBUF.
trigger: Byte-wise mask or index ops that would be FP32 on VectorE.
fix: Map int8/int16 element work to GpSimd instructions.

rule: For MX on trn3: groups of 32 contraction elements share one uint8 scale; quantize_mx produces MXFP8 (not FP4) from BF16/FP16 in SBUF at 4 elements/partition/cycle; MXFP4 inputs are converted to MXFP8 inside TensorE; MXFP8 x MXFP4 mixing is allowed.
why: OCP microscaling as implemented by NeuronCore-v4 TensorE/VectorE.
trigger: Designing an on-device quantization pipeline.
fix: Quantize activations with nisa.quantize_mx; keep FP4 weights quantized offline.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium3_arch.rst :: MX data-type Quantization; nki/deep-dives/mxfp-matmul.rst :: What is MXFP4/8

rule: Use TF32 (8-bit exponent, 10-bit mantissa) when FP32 range with more mantissa than BF16 is needed; it runs at BF16 matmul speed on TensorE.
why: TF32 is listed with BF16/FP16/FP8 at the same peak (92 TFLOPS trn1, 79 TFLOPS trn2).
trigger: Precision-sensitive matmuls currently in FP32.
fix: Cast to nl.tfloat32 before nc_matmul.
source: about-neuron/arch/neuron-features/data-types.rst :: Trn1 / Inf2; nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Tensor Engine Data Types

rule: When choosing storage dtype for streamed weights, remember the DMA payload floor is in bytes: 2 KiB/partition needs 1024 bf16 or 2048 fp8 elements, so fp8 tiles must be twice as wide to stay DMA-efficient.
why: DMA efficiency depends on bytes per partition, not elements.
trigger: fp8 weight tiles of [128, 1024] (1 KiB/partition).
fix: Widen fp8 tiles to >= 2048 (ideally 4096) elements per partition.
check_sketch: bytes_per_partition check (see dma-4kib-per-partition-target).

rule: Do not chain .ap() calls expecting composition: the outer .ap() addresses raw storage and fully overrides the inner one; use slice/reshape/permute/select views to compose.
why: ap() interprets pattern/offset against the underlying storage, ignoring the view it is called on.
trigger: inner = t.ap(...); outer = inner.ap(...)
fix: t.slice(...).slice(...) or compute one .ap() from the base tensor.
check_sketch: flag .ap() invoked on a tensor that is itself an .ap() result.
source: nki/deep-dives/nki-aps.rst :: Composition and .ap on a view

rule: Write .ap() patterns as [[step, num], ...] from major to minor with the partition tuple first; the profiler displays them in reverse (hardware) order.
why: The NKI pattern order is opposite to what the hardware accepts, so profiler strings like [1,1,1][1,1,1] read minor-first.
trigger: Comparing profiler access patterns to source patterns.
fix: Reverse mentally when reading 'fp32@0x4000[strides][shape]' in Neuron Explorer.
source: nki/deep-dives/nki-aps.rst :: NKI API for the Access Pattern

rule: Allow only one dynamic select per view, never on the partition dim of SBUF/PSUM tensors, and do not further slice the selected dimension.
why: Hardware indirect addressing applies one scalar or vector offset on a single indirect_dim.
trigger: A.select(0, idx).select(1, idx2) or sbuf_tile.select(0, idx).
fix: Resolve one index on device and the rest statically; use NkiTensor.is_indirect() to test.
check_sketch: count dynamic selects per view; check dim != 0 for SBUF/PSUM.

rule: Initialize VirtualRegisters only with immediate ints (nisa.register_alloc(0)) and load runtime values with nisa.register_load(reg, tensor); uninitialized tensors used as loop conditions must be explicitly memset/dma'd.
why: Memory allocation does not initialize; register_alloc takes an optional immediate, not a tensor.
trigger: while reg: loops reading garbage conditions.
fix: zero = nl.zeros((1,1), nl.int32, nl.sbuf); nisa.dma_copy(dst=cond_hbm, src=zero); reg = nisa.register_alloc(1); ... nisa.register_load(reg, cond)
check_sketch: flag register_alloc(tensor) and reads of ndarray never written.
source: nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Direct Hardware Control; Control Flow Constructs

rule: Pass kernel inputs/outputs as HBM tensors; load into SBUF before compute and allocate outputs with buffer=nl.shared_hbm (or nl.hbm).
why: NKI kernel parameters must be HBM references; host memory is not directly accessible.
trigger: Returning an SBUF tile from a kernel.
fix: out = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm); nisa.dma_copy(dst=out, src=sbuf_tile); return out
check_sketch: check return values are HBM-allocated.

rule: In nisa.activation, scale may be a per-partition [P,1] tile or a compile-time scalar, but bias must be a [P,1] SBUF/PSUM tile (one element per partition).
why: The ScalarE multiply-add stage reads one scale/bias value per lane.
trigger: Passing a scalar bias or a full-width bias tile.
fix: Materialize bias as a [128,1] tile (e.g. nl.full) before the activation.
check_sketch: check bias operand shape == (P,1).

rule: Feed nisa.quantize_mx from SBUF only (not PSUM) and write both data and scale outputs to SBUF; the source must already be in the interleaved MX layout.
why: VectorE quantization preserves layout and cannot read PSUM in this instruction.
trigger: quantize_mx directly on a PSUM matmul output.
fix: Evict PSUM with a strided tensor_copy that also interleaves, then quantize.
check_sketch: flag quantize_mx with PSUM src.
source: nki/deep-dives/mxfp-matmul.rst :: Quantize-MX + Matmul-MX; nki/guides/architecture/trainium3_arch.rst :: MX data-type Quantization

rule: Do not plan trn3 kernels around Activation2 (max/min/absmax reductions, bias subtract), SBUF/PSUM indirect gather/scatter for compute engines, DMA read-add-write, or DMA traffic shaping: these hardware features had no nki.isa API in these docs.
why: The Trainium3 guide explicitly notes missing nki.isa support for each.
trigger: Designing for trn3 free-dim gathers in SBUF.
fix: Emulate with multiple instructions (one per non-uniform vector) until APIs ship.
source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium3_arch.rst :: More flexible nisa.activation; SBUF/PSUM indirect access; SBUF Read-Add-Write; DMA Traffic Shaping

rule: Use plain Python range() for compile-time loops; nl.static_range, nl.affine_range and nl.sequential_range are deprecated aliases that also unroll at specialization.
why: Loops over range() are unrolled with the loop variable a compile-time constant, enabling meta-programming; only dynamic_range runs on device.
trigger: New code using affine_range to hint parallelism.
fix: for i in range(n): ... ; for runtime bounds use nl.dynamic_range.
source: nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Scheduling options for loops / Control Flow Constructs; nki/deep-dives/nki-dynamic-loops.rst

rule: Target Trainium2 (NeuronCore-v3) and Trainium3 (v4) for new NKI kernels; trn1/inf2 docs remain for architectural grounding but the FAQ lists only Trn2/Trn3 as supported.
why: The FAQ states NKI supports Trainium2 and Trainium3; the architecture index still lists Trainium/Inferentia2 as supported generations (doc inconsistency).
trigger: Choosing NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE and feature set.
fix: Set os.environ['NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE']='trn2' in standalone tests.
source: nki/nki_faq.rst :: Which AWS chips does NKI support?; nki/guides/architecture/index.rst

rule: When writing .ap() on SBUF/PSUM tensors make pattern[0] == [prod(free dims), num_partitions] and treat offset as element offset within the flattened storage; dtype= reinterpret-casts and requires recomputing element counts.
why: Access patterns are loops over flattened storage; partition access must be contiguous; view() handles the last-dim scaling automatically for casts.
trigger: Hand-written ap patterns for a (128, 2, 64) tile.
fix: t.ap(pattern=[[128, 128],[1, 64]], offset=...) for a (128,128) tensor; use t.view(nl.bfloat16) for bit casts.
check_sketch: validate pattern[0][0] == prod(t.shape[1:]).
source: nki/deep-dives/nki-aps.rst :: Semantics / Reinterpret Cast with ap

rule: Set NEURON_FRAMEWORK_DEBUG=1 (save NEFF), XLA_IR_DEBUG=1 and XLA_HLO_DEBUG=1 before compiling to get profiler source mapping, then capture with neuron-explorer capture --profile-nth-exec=2.
why: The NEFF carries instructions and debug metadata; the second execution avoids one-time warmup effects.
trigger: Preparing a profile.
fix: neuron-explorer capture -n ./compiler_workdir/graph.neff -s profile.ntff --profile-nth-exec=2; neuron-explorer view --data-path ./ws (ports 3001/3002).

rule: Set NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE=trn2 (or trn3) when compiling kernels on a host without the target device so generation-specific features (hwdge, double FP8, transpose mode) are selected.
why: Tutorial kernels set this at import; the compiler chooses DGE modes and instruction variants by target.
trigger: Compiling on a CPU-only box.
fix: os.environ['NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE'] = 'trn2'

rule: Control graph-level precision with --auto-cast / --auto-cast-type (FP32 -> BF16 by default) and integer behavior with --native-int64 (trn2+) and --implicit-integer-downcast.
why: The Neuron compiler auto-converts FP32 models to BF16 and 64-bit ints to 32-bit unless told otherwise; accuracy should be benchmarked.
trigger: Unexpected bf16 inputs arriving at a kernel expecting fp32, or int64 indices truncated.
fix: Pass explicit compiler_args in torch_neuronx.trace.
source: about-neuron/arch/neuron-features/data-types.rst :: Model Type Conversion; Integer Type Conversion

rule: Expect the NKI compiler to keep your instruction order, allocation and engine choices; it only does light middle/back-end passes and is inserted late into the graph compile.
why: NKI is compiled per kernel to NKI IR (MLIR) and spliced into the Neuron IR late so the Graph Compiler cannot undo kernel decisions.
trigger: Relying on the graph compiler to fix a poorly scheduled kernel.
fix: Optimize explicitly in the kernel (engine selection, tile sizes, buffering).

rule: Expect recompiles to hit the on-disk Neuron Persistent Cache at /var/tmp/neuron-compile-cache; clear it when changing kernels that produce identical graph hashes.
why: torch-neuronx caches compiled NEFFs by graph hash across runs.
trigger: Stale kernel behavior after edits.
fix: Remove the cache entry or change the graph.

rule: Drive optimization until the Summary tab shows either a compute engine >= 90% active (compute-bound) or MBU >= 60% (memory-bound); matmul kernels should also approach 100% MFU.
why: These are the practical 'done' thresholds the performance guide uses; 100% is the ideal.
trigger: Summary tab engine/dma_active_time_percent, MBU, MFU.
fix: If neither threshold is met, follow Opt #1-#10 in order: arithmetic intensity, engine idle gaps, engine efficiency, DMA efficiency.

rule: Diagnose each engine idle gap by the semaphore wait of the first instruction after it: a semaphore named after an engine (Vector/Scalar/GpSimd/Tensor) means a cross-engine dependency; a name starting with q means a DMA (qSyncIO* = loads, qSyncSpillReload* = spills).
why: Compiler-inserted semaphores encode data dependencies; the wait condition identifies the producer.
trigger: Visible idle gaps on the bottleneck engine.
fix: Engine wait -> tile the pipeline (Opt #3); DMA wait -> prefetch/overlap (Opt #4) or fix DMA efficiency (Opt #9); spill wait -> fuse (Opt #2).
source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Reducing engine idle time / Opt #3 / Opt #4

rule: Sort the Tensor Info widget by 'Load to SBUF Repeat Factor'; any input with factor well above 1 is being reloaded and should be cached in SBUF or its loops reordered.
why: Repeat factor = bytes loaded into SBUF / tensor size; e.g. a 32 KiB tensor loaded 512 KiB over 16 DMAs has factor 16.
trigger: Repeat factor >> 1 on large inputs.
fix: Hoist loads, reorder loops (Mamba tutorial), or block so the reused operand stays resident.

rule: Recognize overhead-bound engines by repeated instructions with one-element access patterns (e.g. fp32@0x4000[1,1,1][1,1,1]) and src==prior dst; measured II ~222 ns on NC-v3.
why: Each such instruction does ~1 cycle of work under ~100+ cycles of overhead plus RAW stalls.
trigger: ScalarE/VectorE busy with thousands of tiny TENSOR_SCALAR instructions.
fix: Increase free size per instruction or use a scan/fused instruction.

rule: Check the channels= field on vector instructions and the '128*N' operand on MATMUL; values below 128 indicate idle lanes/PE columns to recover via partition vectorization.
why: Lane and column usage are directly encoded in instruction operands.
trigger: channels=64; MATMUL 128*96.
fix: Stack tiles across partitions; widen stationary free size to 128.

rule: If LDWEIGHTS (LoadStationary) shows 1 element/partition while MATMUL shows 128+ elements/partition back-to-back, swap stationary and moving operands.
why: This is the matrix-vector 'short stationary' pattern that loses Fast LoadStationary.
trigger: Decode GEMV kernels.
fix: nc_matmul(stationary=weights, moving=vector).

rule: Switch the DMA view to per-engine transfers; if gaps between bars exceed the bars or hover shows tiny sizes (32 B), transfers are too small.
why: Each transfer shows as a continuous bar; overhead appears as empty gaps. Good kernels show ~85% DMA utilization.
trigger: DMA engines 'busy' but MBU < 60%.
fix: Enlarge free/partition dims of nl.load/nl.store.

rule: Use the profiler search to highlight DMA activities performing transposes; if they take substantial time in a memory-bound kernel, move the transpose to TensorE.
why: load_transpose2d / dma_transpose run at reduced DMA bandwidth.
trigger: Transposing DMAs on the critical path.
fix: See dma-avoid-load-transpose2d-memory-bound.

rule: Classify the kernel by comparing dma_active_time_percent with the busiest engine: DMA ~100% and TensorE < 90% (e.g. 99.93% vs 87.28%) means memory-bound; after blocking the tutorial reached DMA 21.5% / TensorE 99.5%.
why: Active-time percentages in the Summary tab summarize which resource is saturated.
trigger: Deciding between compute and data-movement optimizations.
fix: Memory-bound -> Opt #9/#10 and blocking; compute-bound -> Opt #5-#8.

rule: When TensorE shows clear idle gaps while VectorE or ScalarE is busy at every instant (typical self-attention inner loop), optimize by instruction combining and engine rebalancing, not matmul tuning.
why: Attention is vector/scalar heavy; the bottleneck engines are VectorE/ScalarE.
trigger: Profile fig19 pattern.
fix: activation with fused scale/bias, activation_reduce, DMA SBUF2SBUF transposes, trn3 VectorE exponential.

rule: Spill/reload DMAs have no nki_source_location; identify the spilled tensor by its name in the DMA details (e.g. inst__I-35-0:a_dst_L3_sg0000, Source [[TMPBUF]] -> Dest [SB]).
why: The compiler generates spill traffic from SBUF usage analysis, not from an explicit API call.
trigger: Instruction blocked on qSyncSpillReload0.
fix: Map the tensor name back to the kernel variable and reduce its live range or size.

rule: Upload kernel source with the NEFF/NTFF (or rely on the filename:line in instruction details) and Cmd/Ctrl-click instructions to jump to the NKI line and highlight all related instructions.
why: Neuron Explorer links device instructions to NKI source locations when debug env vars are set.
trigger: Attributing hot instructions to code.
fix: Add Widget -> Code Editor; hover instruction -> Cmd+click.

rule: Write a custom NKI kernel only for (a) hot regions where the Neuron Compiler's general-purpose lowering under-utilizes hardware, or (b) operators the compiler does not support; otherwise use compiler output or NKI-Lib kernels.
why: The compiler already inserts optimized NKI kernels for common ops (vLLM/NxDI models use them); NKI-Lib ships attention, MLP, RMSNorm+quant and collective kernels that beat compiler-generated code.
trigger: Profiler shows engines idle waiting on DMA or gaps in a frequently executed section.
fix: Pick a 'minimum cut' subgraph with few inputs/outputs; validate against a numpy reference with representative sizes before optimizing.

rule: Expect dense GEMM, CONV and PF-transpose to be handled well by the compiler on TensorE; spend custom-kernel effort on fusion, layout and data movement around them rather than re-implementing the matmul itself.
why: TensorE is 'highly optimized for GEMM, CONV, and Transpose' and holds >90% of core FLOPS; the tutorial matmul reaches 99.5% TensorE utilization only through blocking/DMA work, not instruction tricks.
trigger: Planning a kernel that is mostly a dense matmul.
fix: Focus on hoisting loads, blocking all three dims, PSUM bank rotation and output coalescing.

rule: Treat gather/scatter/indirect patterns (embedding lookups, paged KV cache, interpolation, grid-sample) as the hardest class to make fast: they require software DGE on GpSimd, hwdge cannot gather, and before trn3 no compute engine can gather along the free dim in SBUF.
why: Indirect DMA is swdge-only (GpSimd generates descriptors into SBUF); per-row gathers produce small payloads that are descriptor-rate and overhead bound; non-uniform in-SBUF access needs one instruction per vector until NeuronCore-v4 indirect access (no API yet).
trigger: Kernels dominated by vector_offset DMAs or many tiny per-index copies.
fix: Restructure data so indices select large contiguous blocks (>= 2 KiB per partition), gather 128 rows per DMA, hoist index generation, and keep GpSimd otherwise idle; consider precomputing gathered layouts on the host.
check_sketch: count dma ops with vector_offset and their bytes per descriptor.

rule: For auto-regressive decode GEMV, keep the large weight tile as stationary ([K=128, M=128] per instruction) and the token vector(s) as moving, and batch tokens/heads into the moving free dim where possible.
why: Fast LoadStationary makes weight loads cheap and the small moving tile issues at the 64-cycle turnaround; TensorE is otherwise starved by the 1-column output.
trigger: Single-token matmuls over large weights.
fix: nc_matmul(stationary=W_tile[K,128], moving=x[K, n_tokens]); evict transposed output.

rule: For linear -> RMSNorm -> linear chains keep weights stationary and reduce the squared sum across partitions on TensorE; for linear -> LayerNorm swap operands so bn_stats sees features on the free dim.
why: bn_stats must reduce along the free dim; RMSNorm's sum can go either way, so choose the layout the following matmul needs ([4H, seq]).
trigger: PF transposes between matmul and normalization.
fix: Apply technique 1 (operand swap) for LayerNorm, technique 2 (engine choice) for RMSNorm.

rule: Map softmax as: max-subtract+exp on ScalarE (activation with bias=-max), row sums on VectorE (or activation_reduce), reciprocal scaling on ScalarE, causal mask on GpSimd; on trn3 use VectorE nisa.exponential.
why: This split keeps every engine busy in the attention pipeline and uses fused instructions.
trigger: Attention kernels.
fix: Pipeline per 128-row tile; avoid TensorE for anything but the two matmuls.

rule: Avoid TensorE 'alternative uses' (transpose, broadcast, cross-partition sum, shuffles) inside matmul-bound kernels; use them freely in normalization/softmax kernels where TensorE is idle.
why: These ops keep TensorE from useful high-throughput work; they are acceptable only when matmuls are not the bottleneck or layout conflicts are unavoidable.
trigger: TensorE transpose share high in a matmul-heavy profile.
fix: Move reshapes to VectorE/DMA or fix layouts upstream.

rule: Implement sequential recurrences (Mamba prefix scan, cumulative products) with nisa.tensor_tensor_scan rather than per-timestep tensor_scalar loops.
why: The naive implementation issues seq_len dependent one-element instructions (~222 ns each); the scan instruction processes the whole free dim in one pipelined instruction.
trigger: Loop over sequence positions updating a [128,1] state.
fix: nisa.tensor_tensor_scan on VectorE (see Fused Mamba tutorial).
check_sketch: flag loops over a sequence dim with single-column tensor_scalar updates.

rule: Choose kernel IO tensor layouts in HBM to match the first consuming instruction's partition requirement and to keep DMAs contiguous; IO transposes are a layout decision, not a hardware necessity.
why: A [out_ch, in_ch] weight consumed by nc_matmul as [in_ch, out_ch] needs either a TensorE transpose per tile or a low-bandwidth DMA transpose; delivering it pre-transposed from the framework removes both.
trigger: nl.matmul(transpose_x=False) or nc_transpose right after every load.
fix: Expose a transposed weight layout at the framework boundary (weight.t() once) as the tutorial's lhsT does.
check_sketch: flag transposes whose input is a kernel parameter.

rule: Estimate the batch size at which decode/inference becomes compute-bound as ceil(0.5 x (PeakFLOPS/MemBW) / (model FLOPs per sample / (params x dtype bytes))); below it the kernel is weight-bandwidth bound and DMA rules dominate.
why: Arithmetic intensity grows linearly with batch; the roofline ridge is PeakFLOPS/MemBW (BERT-Large bf16 on trn1: batch 2).
trigger: Deciding whether a decode kernel should be tuned for DMA or TensorE.
fix: For batch=1 LLM decode assume memory-bound: maximize bytes/partition per DMA, use both LNC cores, keep weights bf16/fp8.
check_sketch: ai_per_sample = flops/(params*bytes); ridge = peak_flops/mem_bw.

rule: Explicitly initialize any SBUF/PSUM/HBM tensor that is read before being fully written (accumulators, loop conditions): nl.ndarray does not zero memory.
why: Allocation only reserves space; the tutorial memsets fp32 result tiles before tensor_tensor accumulation and zeroes the loop-condition tensor via DMA.
trigger: Accumulating with op=add into a freshly allocated tile, or nl.zeros expected from ndarray.
fix: nisa.memset(dst=tile, value=0.0) or nl.zeros(...).
check_sketch: dataflow: flag reads of an allocation with no prior full write.

rule: When reusing a PSUM tile across accumulation groups, be explicit with accumulate=False on the first matmul of each group (or allocate a fresh PSUM tile per group).
why: Default auto-detection treats the first write to a PSUM location as overwrite and subsequent writes as accumulate; reuse without a clear 'first write' risks accumulating onto stale data.
trigger: Loop that reuses one psum buffer for multiple output tiles without nl.zeros.
fix: nisa.nc_matmul(dst=psum, ..., accumulate=False) for k==0, accumulate=True otherwise.
check_sketch: track PSUM allocation reuse across independent output tiles.

rule: Never use a dynamic_range loop variable in host-side Python logic (if i == 0, shape math); it is a device register.
why: The loop body is emitted once and iterated by hardware, so the variable has no compile-time value.
trigger: if i == 0: inside dynamic_range.
fix: Use device-side conditionals (register compares) or peel the first iteration statically.
check_sketch: AST: dynamic loop var used in Python control flow or arithmetic feeding shapes.

rule: Pad the contraction dim to a multiple of 2 (zeros) before using double-row FP8 matmul; both operands' second dim must be exactly 2.
why: The hardware pairs two K-halves per PE; an odd K would read uninitialized data.
trigger: K % 2 != 0 with perf_mode=double_row.
fix: memset the padding slice to 0 in both stationary and moving tiles.
check_sketch: check shape[1]==2 and padded regions zeroed.

rule: For MX matmul, pack the four elements that were 128 apart along K into adjacent free-dim slots (interleave) before quantize_mx; feeding row-contiguous data gives wrong results, not an error.
why: nc_matmul_mx assumes each _x4 element holds K positions k, k+128, k+256, k+384 and the scale for its 8P x 4F group.
trigger: MX kernels verified only against nc_matmul_mx_golden with pre-packed inputs.
fix: Use copy_data_strided-style tensor_copy to build [128, F, 4] from [4,128,F]; validate against the golden model.
check_sketch: compare against the reference packing in the tutorial.

rule: Use nki device_print (or nki.simulate) to inspect runtime values; ordinary print() in a kernel executes during compilation only.
why: Most NKI code runs at specialization; only nki.isa calls become device instructions.
trigger: Debug prints that never show per-iteration values.
fix: Build kernels incrementally and verify small operators in simulation mode.

rule: Know that nl.matmul(x, y) with transpose_x=False (or nisa.nc_matmul high-level form on [M,K]) silently inserts a TensorE transpose of x; pass pre-transposed operands to avoid hidden cost.
why: nc_matmul(x, y) for [M,K] inputs is a two-step nc_transpose + matmul.
trigger: Unexpected transpose instructions in the profile after a plain matmul call.
fix: Provide x as [K,M] (lhsT) and call nisa.nc_matmul(stationary=xT, moving=y).
check_sketch: flag nl.matmul without transposed LHS in hot loops.

rule: Account for Trainium2's additional SBUF layouts (row-major, col-major-2B, col-major-4B) and strong-order-write DMA barriers when reasoning about DMA transposes and write ordering.
why: The Trainium2 hardware page lists these as data-movement improvements over Trainium1 (write-after-write barriers), underpinning DMA transpose for 2-byte and 4-byte dtypes.
trigger: Designing transposed loads for 1-byte dtypes.
fix: Use 2- or 4-byte dtypes for DMA transposes.

rule: Do not take the performance guide's 'NKI only supports running a kernel on a single NeuronCore' note at face value; the LNC guide and FAQ document kernel[2] launches on two physical cores.
why: The docs were updated at different times; the LNC page (12/2025) and FAQ are newer.
trigger: Deciding whether to shard a decode kernel across cores.
fix: Use kernel[2] with program_id sharding on trn2/trn3.
